state.coordinates: The boat is at (0,0), facing forward. target.forward_m is metres ahead (+) or behind (-); target.left_m is metres left (+) or right (-). Positive yaw rate and angular acceleration mean counterclockwise (left) rotation. These coordinates describe the state at the start of the requested action.
state.motion: Acceleration commands take effect immediately when simulation resumes. Speed derivative = longitudinal command - linear damping * speed; yaw-rate derivative = angular command - angular damping * yaw rate. Yaw rate changes heading; signed speed moves the boat along its changing heading, with no independent sideways drift. The target is fixed in the world; its boat-relative coordinates change as the boat moves and turns. Speeds are clamped to their limits. Zero commands allow damping to slow motion; they do not stop it instantly.

action.instructions: The CURRENT target is the FINAL PARKING REGION. Complete the task by being inside the circle defined by target.arrival_radius_m AND having abs(boat.speed_mps) <= target.stop_speed_mps at the same time. The stop-speed threshold applies INSIDE the circle, not throughout the approach. While far outside, make forward progress toward the circle; do not creep at the final stop speed or repeatedly brake an already slow boat. If current motion would stop well short of the circle, positive thrust is needed to keep approaching. As the circle gets close, reduce excess forward momentum early enough to stop inside it instead of overshooting and turning back. Brake when existing speed threatens to overshoot, including when the target is off to one side; steer and brake together when needed. Examples: forward_m=8, left_m=0, speed_mps=0.1 needs positive thrust to approach, not braking or coasting to a halt. forward_m=1.5, left_m=0, speed_mps=2 needs braking. forward_m=1.8, left_m=1.5, speed_mps=3.8 needs braking while steering, not more forward thrust. Pilot the boat into the CURRENT target circle using one combined longitudinal and angular acceleration input. Target coordinates are relative to the present boat: forward_m>0 is ahead; forward_m<0 is behind. left_m>0 is LEFT; left_m<0 is RIGHT. Positive speed travels forward; negative speed travels backward. Positive longitudinal input increases signed speed. Negative input brakes forward motion but makes backward motion faster. Positive input brakes backward motion. Positive yaw_rate_deg_s means already turning LEFT; negative means already turning RIGHT. Positive angular input increases LEFT rotation; negative increases RIGHT rotation. Inputs change yaw rate, not heading instantly. Steer toward the target side, but brake existing rotation before passing alignment. Zero angular input does not stop rotation instantly. A target behind calls for turning back rather than charging forward. Commands take effect immediately, but speed and yaw rate change over time; yaw rate changes heading, and speed moves the boat along that changing heading. The target is stationary in the world, so its relative coordinates change as the boat moves and turns. Account for damping even with zero input. Consider the travel and heading change throughout the action interval, not just the current side of the target. At high speed, turning alone may miss a nearby circle: reduce forward speed while steering when needed. Examples: forward_m=10,left_m=5,target ahead-left, requires left steering. forward_m=10,left_m=-5 requires right steering. forward_m=-3,left_m=4,target behind-left: turn left while limiting forward travel away. forward_m=10,left_m=0,yaw_rate_deg_s=20: brake LEFT rotation with NEGATIVE angular input. forward_m=10,left_m=0,yaw_rate_deg_s=-20: brake RIGHT rotation with POSITIVE angular input. Choose exactly one pair, held for the requested interval. Prefer approaching while moving forward: if currently moving backward, use positive longitudinal input to arrest backward travel before progressing forward. When a target is far to the side or behind, keep turning toward it; do not brake that turn merely because yaw is nonzero. Rotational braking is for impending alignment, not for a target still far from the bow direction. Which ONE combined longitudinal and angular acceleration command best achieves this target's completion condition for the next 0.4 seconds? The supplied state is measured at the start of this interval.

criteria.negative_full__clockwise_full: LONGITUDINAL situation: Strongly reduce signed speed. Brake substantial forward motion when continued travel would overshoot the stop circle or carry the boat away while turning. With backward speed, this increases backward motion; continued braking past zero causes reverse travel. ANGULAR situation: Target far RIGHT of the bow (negative left_m, or behind-right); strong clockwise turning is needed. Alternatively, target nearly straight AHEAD and substantial LEFT yaw needs strong braking. Commands: longitudinal -1.5 m/s^2; angular -60 deg/s^2. Both situations must fit.
